claims.text: Unmodified TC4 is a Ti6Al4V alloy with an alpha-plus-beta dual-phase microstructure.
Unmodified TC4 has low hardness and poor wear resistance.
A TiAl-based composite coating containing in situ formed TiC particles and minor Cu can be deposited on TC4 by laser cladding.
The TiAl coating matrix will form a strong metallurgical bond with the TC4 substrate.
Dispersed fine TiC particles and Cu will produce a refined composite surface microstructure.
Minor Cu addition will strengthen the TiAl-based matrix by solid-solution strengthening.
Hard TiC particles will hinder plastic deformation.
Hard TiC particles will reduce abrasive wear.
The combined TiC reinforcement and Cu-modified TiAl matrix will increase coating hardness.
The combined TiC reinforcement and Cu-modified TiAl matrix will improve wear resistance.
The coated TC4 surface will have approximately 50% or greater hardness than untreated TC4.
The coated sample will have a lower wear rate than untreated TC4 under high-load conditions.
The coating will retain bulk properties similar to untreated TC4, including weight and corrosion resistance.
The expected improvement applies under high-contact dry or minimally lubricated sliding conditions while the coating remains stable and adherent.
Excessive cladding-induced residual stress or coating delamination during thermal cycling may prevent the expected improvement.
The optimum TiC and Cu concentrations and microstructural parameters are not yet determined.
The coating's long-term stability under cyclic thermal and mechanical loads remains undetermined.
